vintage: DOSM LFS 2021 workers by state, apportioned by 2020 district GDP

rule.text: A district appears when the workers in its industries have a location quotient (the city's share of workers in them divided by Malaysia's share) of at least 1.25 and number at least 1,000 or 1% of the city's workers. Districts are ranked by how many workers they have above the national norm (workers minus workers divided by the quotient); up to 5 per city. The city type is named after the strongest district, or after a listed district with a quotient of at least 6 and at least 3% of the city's workers when there is one; 'Capital city' goes only to Kuala Lumpur. These are the U.S. edition's rules, with two differences: DOSM publishes no detailed industries, so a district is a whole industry section and no speciality can qualify; and the worker counts are estimates, not counts. DOSM's Labour Force Survey gives workers by industry for each state (2021) and M2 shares them over the state's districts by their 2020 GDP in the same sector (agriculture, mining, manufacturing, construction, services), so every city in a state has that state's mix of service industries and differs from its neighbours only in how large its services sector is. Read a district as 'this state's industry, concentrated in this city', not as a count of the city's own workers. Harbor, Aerodrome and Encampment districts are not drawn: DOSM publishes no ports, aviation or defence workers.
rule.county_note: Districts (daerah) get no industry districts in the Malaysian edition.
